item.title: Vatican names first laywoman to head communications
item.description: The Vatican has appointed 39-year-old Mexican-American media executive, Maria Alvarado, as its new head of communications, making her the first laywoman and first non-Italian to lead the department. Alvarado, who assumes office this week, will oversee the Vatican’s television, radio and print operations, as well as its press office. Her appointment, announced in June by Pope Leo XIV, marks a significant development in the Church’s leadership structure, where senior positions traditionally held by women have largely been occupied by nuns. Alvarado, popularly known as Montse, said her appointment came directly from the Pope rather than through a conventional recruitment process. “I didn’t apply; I wasn’t chosen” through a standard application process, she said in an interview with EWTN News, where she has served as president and chief operating officer since 2023. “It was an appointment from the Holy Father,” she added. EWTN News is the news division of the Eternal Word Television Network, the largest Catholic television network in the United States. Founded by a nun, the network has become an influential platform among conservative Catholics. However, some of its programmes have had a strained relationship with the Vatican, particularly during the papacy of Pope Francis, whose reform agenda attracted criticism from sections of the Church’s conservative wing. In 2021, Francis appeared to criticise the network, lamenting what he described as a major Catholic television channel that was constantly criticising the Pope. Alvarado was a presenter for EWTN at the time. Born in Mexico, Alvarado moved to the United States as a child and grew up in Miami before relocating to Washington for her studies. She spent 14 years working at the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty, a non-profit law firm specialising in the defence of religious freedom, before taking charge of EWTN News in 2023. At EWTN, she oversaw international media platforms producing content in seven languages across television, print, radio, digital media and social networks. Alvarado said she had not originally envisaged a career in media and communications, explaining that her ambition had been to get married and have children. She was previously married, but the marriage was subsequently annulled by the Catholic Church. She succeeds 70-year-old Paolo Ruffini, who was appointed by Pope Francis in 2018 and became the first layperson to head a Vatican dicastery, the Church’s equivalent of a government ministry. Lucetta Scaraffia, founder of the Vatican women’s magazine, Women Church World, and a professor of history at Rome’s La Sapienza University, described Alvarado’s appointment as a recognition of her professional abilities. “This is a woman who has been chosen for her skills and her qualities,” Scaraffia told AFP. She said Alvarado’s appointment as the first non-Italian to head the department would bring a different approach and a more international outlook to Vatican communications. Scaraffi

item.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
item.description: Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday. Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice. As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to “finish the job”. Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was “about protecting people”. “A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country,” he said, according to a written version of his statement. “The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat.” He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC. It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: “no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone”. When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line. The agreement’s Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments. “PABS is the last remaining piece of our puzzle,” Tedros said. During the Covid pandemic, he highlighted that “the world developed vaccines in record time, but too many countries were left waiting while others secured far more than they needed”. “That inequity cost lives, prolonged the pandemic and increased the risk of new variants emerging.” Completing the final piece of the pandemic treaty, he insisted, was “the key that will unlock the door to a safer future”. item.title: Court delivers judgment in alleged terrorism financing case against Tukur Mamu
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday fixed Jan. 27, 2027, for judgment in a charge filed by the Federal Government against Tukur Mamu, alleged terrorists’ negotiator during the Abuja-Kaduna train attack hostages in 2022. Justice Mohammed Umar fixed the date after the Federal Government’s lawyer, David Kaswe, and Mamu’s counsel, Johnson Usman, SAN, adopted their final written addresses and presented their arguments for and against the case. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Mamu, who was arrested on Sept. 7, 2022 by the Egyptian security officials at the Cairo International Airport, was earlier arraigned on a 10-count charge bordering on terrorism financing. However, the prosecution amended the counts by bringing in more offences, including unlawful possession of firearms without valid licence and money laundering charges. When the case was called on Monday, Usman informed the court that the case was scheduled for the adoption of the parties’ final written addresses. The senior lawyer said the defendant’s final written address was dated July 22 but filed July 23. “Our reply on points of law is dated Oct. 30 and filed the same day. “We adopt these two addresses, and we humbly urge this honourable court to graciously acquit and discharge the defendant on all the counts preferred by the Federal Government as the same, having not been proven in any manner,” he prayed. Usman argued that though the defence team had consistently demanded the licence of the rifle allegedly recovered from Mamu’s residence, the lawyer said the prosecution had failed to produce the licence in court. “You mean the expired licence?” Justice Umar asked Usman. Responding, Usman submitted that their contention was that the licence had not expired as of the time Mamu was arrested. He said even though the prosecution took custody of the arms and the licence, their failure to produce the licence in court had raised serious issues of doubt. He, therefore, urged the court to resolve the issue in favour of his client. “My lord, if my vehicle licence expires and my car is parked at home, the VIO cannot arrest me. ”We have asked for this three consecutive times, but they failed to produce it in court,” he said. But Kaswe, as assistant director, who appeared for the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) on behalf of the Federal Government, disagreed with Usman’s submission. The prosecution lawyer recalled that the licence and the rifle had already been tendered before the court. “My Lord, the record of this court will show that we have tendered the licence together with the arms on the day the PW-5, an exhibit keeper, was led on evidence,” he added. Kaswe reminded us that after the prosecution applied for a safekeeping of the rifle and other exhibits, the court granted their request. item.title: Constitution amendment must protect IGP, CPs from abuse — Okiro
item.description: Former Inspector-General of Police and one-time Chairman of the Police Service Commission, Sir Mike Okiro, in this interview, speaks on the proposed establishment of state police, funding, training and safeguards against possible abuse by state governors. The amendment to Section 214 of the 1999 Constitution on State Police has received the concurrence of about 30 State Houses of Assembly. But one of the core issues is funding, especially given the paucity of funds. How do you think this can be addressed? When the amendment receives presidential assent, the dual police structure will come into effect. From then on, state governments will have to fund the respective police forces in their states. They have to source the funds. After all, they have been supporting the Nigeria Police Force all these years. As a Commissioner of Police in Lagos and Benue states, and later as the IGP, I can attest to the operational and funding support given to the police by state governments. A number of them purchase patrol vehicles for most of the state, area commands and divisions in their respective states. Some, like Lagos, have set up State Security Trust Funds for this purpose. So, I have no doubt in my mind that they will do this effectively. Like I said before, Lagos State, which established Operation Sweep 30 years ago, has demonstrated that it is possible. It has the Lagos State Security Trust Fund, a state-of-the-art surveillance system, as well as a world-class Forensic Analysis Centre. For over 30 years, Lagos has been equipping Operation Sweep, which morphed into the Rapid Response Squad (RRS), with modern vehicles and communication equipment. It even has drones and, I think, a helicopter for policing. So, the state is ready. Similarly, Enugu State also has a state-of-the-art Command and Control Centre, known as the Enugu State Digital Surveillance Control Centre, for effective surveillance of the state. The sophisticated security infrastructure, which comes with facilities for DNA analysis, is aimed at promoting scientific, evidence-based justice and the war against crime. You see, security is essential to all aspects of development. In fact, it is the pivot around which all aspects of development, social, educational and economic, revolve. No investor will invest resources in an unsafe state, and that makes security very crucial. Besides, Chapter Two of the Nigerian Constitution says that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government. That makes it incumbent on federal and state governments to ensure this to the letter. I agree that some governors are grappling with the regular payment of salaries to teachers and nurses. I know state police will be one of the essential services in any state. If a governor cannot pay teachers, he must still pay the police. item.title: Catholic Priest leads congregation in song for Obi, Kwankwaso
item.description: A Catholic priest has been filmed leading worshippers in a church service in a song endorsing Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a video circulating on X, the priest is seen leading members of the congregation in singing a song rendered in Igbo, describing the NDC as a better political platform. The priest sang: “Party Peter Obi ka mma; Party Kwankwaso, ka mma!” meaning “Peter Obi’s party is better; Kwankwaso’s party is better.” The video has drawn attention to the growing involvement of religious leaders in political conversations ahead of the 2027 elections, with some publicly expressing support for candidates while others have criticised particular political arrangements. In August, Islamic cleric, Sani Jingir, reportedly urged Muslims to vote for a Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket in the 2027 election. Jingir made the call at a mass wedding organised by the Kano State Government for 1,500 couples, where he urged Muslims to vote in a manner that would reflect their numerical strength in the country. President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who are both Muslims, currently occupy the country’s two highest executive offices. Nigeria has an informal tradition of balancing presidential tickets along religious lines, usually pairing a Muslim presidential candidate with a Christian running mate. Kwankwaso had condemned Jingir’s remarks in a post on X. In another development, the Charismatic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office. The endorsement was announced during the group’s 2026 synod in Abuja, attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris. Representatives of the conference from the six geopolitical zones reportedly mandated its President-General, Leonard Kawas, to announce the decision. Kawas said the CBCN had members in 52 countries, including 950 canonical bishops in Nigeria. He recalled that the conference was among religious organisations that expressed concerns over the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket adopted by the All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general elections. However, he said Tinubu had surprised the group through the appointment of Christians to key positions in his administration. According to him, the president had demonstrated an ability to accommodate Nigeria’s diversity. “We are here today to reassure him of our solid support. We are standing with him in prayers and advocacy for the good programmes he has brought forth for the liberation of Nigeria,” Kawas said. “We stand with the president today, and as long as he is willing to be our president and even come in 2027, we will still be standing with him.” The post Catholic Priest leads congregation in song for Obi, Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kyari: 33.5m food insecurity projection not political forecast
item.description: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has cautioned opposition politicians against using the October 2026 Cadre Harmonisé food security assessment for political propaganda ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kyari, in a statement on Monday, said the projection that 33.5 million Nigerians could face severe food and nutrition insecurity between June and August 2027 should not be interpreted as an assessment of the performance or electoral prospects of any political administration. He described attempts by opposition voices to link the projection to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a misrepresentation of the technical assessment. The minister explained that the Cadre Harmonisé was developed by the Permanent Inter-State Committee for Drought Control in the Sahel (CILSS), alongside regional and technical partners, to identify food and nutrition security risks and enable governments and development partners to respond early. He said the assessment, supported by organisations including the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), World Food Programme (WFP), FEWS NET, UNICEF and the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), was not designed as an election forecast. According to him, the projected figure of 33.5 million represents a decline from the 34.8 million projected for the corresponding period in 2026. Kyari, however, noted that the assessment does not conduct retrospective analysis after the projected period to establish whether the forecasts were accurate. He identified climate change, inconsistent rainfall, prolonged dry spells and disruptions to weather patterns associated with the Super El Niño phenomenon as some of the factors contributing to food and nutrition insecurity. The minister said these challenges had affected planting seasons and crop production, particularly among farmers dependent on rain-fed agriculture. He added that the assessment did not attribute the projected food insecurity figures to the continuation of any particular political administration. Kyari said the Federal Government was responding to the identified risks through expanded access to fertiliser and other agricultural inputs, increased mechanisation, irrigation and dry-season farming, improved agricultural financing, and investments in storage, processing and climate-resilient agriculture. He also highlighted improved security in some farming communities, saying it had enabled farmers who previously could not access their farmlands to resume cultivation. According to him, areas such as Marte and Guzamala in Borno State, which were previously inaccessible to data collectors, have recorded improved stability, allowing the Cadre Harmonisé assessment to be conducted. item.title: Nigerian workers face growing social security risks, NSITF warns
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund, NSITF, has raised the alarm over growing social security risks facing Nigerian workers, warning that the rapid transformation of the labour market through artificial intelligence, AI, automation, digital platforms and the gig economy could leave millions of workers without adequate protection. The Fund has consequently called for urgent measures to close existing social protection gaps, strengthen employer compliance and build a sustainable safety net that guarantees workers’ welfare, dignity and economic security, irrespective of their employment arrangements. The NSITF also emphasised the need for government, employers, organised labour, social security institutions and the media to work together to ensure that technological advancement and changing employment patterns do not create a new generation of economically active but inadequately protected workers. The Managing Director/Chief Executive of NSITF, Oluwaseun Faleye, raised the concerns in his keynote address at the Labour Writers’ Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) Annual Workshop, in Lagos, The address, titled Social Security and Workers’ Welfare in Nigeria’s Political Transition: Closing the Protection Gaps and Building a Sustainable Safety Net, was presented on his behalf by the Deputy General Manager, and Head of Corporate Affairs Department, Alexandra Mede. Faleye described social security as an investment in human dignity, social stability and economic resilience, insisting that its importance should not be measured merely by institutional structures, regulations, financial contributions and statistics. According to him, social security is fundamentally about protecting workers and their families against unforeseen circumstances, including workplace injuries, disabilities, occupational accidents and the sudden loss of a family’s principal breadwinner. He said, “At its heart, social security is about people. It is about the worker who suffers an injury in the course of employment. It is about the family that suddenly loses its principal breadwinner. It is about a worker whose ability to earn an income is affected by an occupational accident.” The NSITF MD/CEO warned that Nigeria’s rapidly changing world of work was creating new challenges for traditional social protection systems, particularly with the growing adoption of technology, artificial intelligence, remote work, automation and digital employment platforms. While acknowledging the opportunities associated with these developments, he expressed concern that workers operating within emerging employment arrangements might be left outside established social protection structures. item.title: Mutfwang vows to protect every inch of Plateau land
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has vowed to protect every inch of the state’s territory, assuring residents that his administration will intensify security efforts and facilitate the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral communities. Mutfwang gave the assurance on Monday in Jos during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council, where he also called on party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said his administration remained committed to protecting communities and preventing further displacement, adding that efforts were underway to strengthen security operations across the state. “If the people of Plateau knew the magnitude of the damage planned against our state, they would appreciate that only God’s intervention and our strategic efforts have helped us thus far. “One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State. “Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities,” he said. Mutfwang disclosed that his administration would deploy additional security personnel, announcing plans to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives the following week. He added that at least 800 trained forest guards would also be deployed within four weeks as part of efforts to strengthen security across the state. “One of the things we have waited for is to get more boots on ground and, by the grace of God, next week we are going to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives. “And in another four weeks, we are going to also release at least 800 trained forest guards. “We are determined to ensure that our people return to their ancestral homes,” the governor said. He commended President Bola Tinubu for what he described as his commitment to the welfare of Nigerians and support for efforts to address insecurity. Mutfwang appealed to residents to remain patient and trust his administration, assuring them that it would continue to work towards restoring peace and security. “And so, all we are asking Plateau people is, trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it,” he said. On the 2027 elections, the governor urged members of the campaign council to take the APC’s message to communities across the state, saying his administration needed another mandate to complete ongoing projects and programmes. He said the campaign would seek the people’s endorsement for a second term to sustain the administration’s development agenda. “We are going to the nooks and crannies of Plateau State to solicit their endorsement and approval for a second time in office because the many things we have begun must not be aborted. “We must ensure that we bring things to a very glorious height,” he said. item.title: Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has approved the payment of a 13th-month pension bonus to all pensioners in the State, as well as a N10,000 one-time welfare support for November, 2026. Governor Umo Eno disclosed this during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, who also endorsed him for re-election in 2027. Governor Eno, who was particularly impressed by their sense of gratitude and quality organisation, assured that the Government under his leadership will continue to prioritize the welfare of pensioners and elderly citizens in the State. “This is indeed humbling to me. It shows that you are truly technocrats with a laudable sense of organization. You may be retired but not tired. I celebrate and appreciate you greatly. “I am now directing that N10,000 be added to the November 2026 pension payment of every pensioner in support of your welfare,” he said. Governor of Akwa Ibom State, Pastor Umo Eno waves to retirees at the meeting. He urged them to equally enroll in the State’s health insurance scheme, which he said was free for 65-year-olds and above, to enable them to enjoy quality healthcare and a good rest across the state. Gov noted that he had promised to clear the backlog of gratuities, stressing that N100 billion has so far been paid, from the accumulated N111 billion since 2012, assuring that before the end of his first term, the balance will be cleared. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to states, which, according to him, has made it possible for him to keep to his promise of clearing the arrears of gratuity. Governor Umo Eno during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners. Earlier, in his welcome remarks, the State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elderly and retired public servants as heartwarming and unprecedented. He also noted that Gov. Eno’s policies have significantly improved their living standard and lifted them from abject poverty to a life of dignity. He expressed gratitude to the Governor for the release of over N100 billion for the payment of inherited gratuities dating back to 2012 and prayed that God will grant the wishes of pensioners by granting him a second term in 2027. Following a motion moved and seconded by Comrade James Inim and Dr. Mrs. Uduak Udoaka, respectively, the pensioners unanimously endorsed President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other candidates of the APC for re-election in 2027. item.title: Dino Melaye throws Quranic citation challenge at Tinubu
item.description: Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest following the President’s recent pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing verses from the Quran after his return to Nigeria. He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back, I challenge him to a Quranic citation competition with me. No one can mock God, SDM.” The challenge comes after Tinubu’s spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed Umrah, the lesser Hajj, and was granted access to enter the Holy Kaaba alongside members of his delegation. In a statement on Monday by Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information & Strategy, Tinubu said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians while reaffirming his commitment to national development and prosperity. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the statement quoted Tinubu. Tinubu also expressed gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Kaaba. Tinubu, reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Quran, said all power and authority belonged to Almighty Allah, who could grant leadership to anyone and take it away at will. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” he said. He also reaffirmed his commitment to national development, declaring, “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people.” On the economy, Tinubu expressed optimism about the country’s progress, saying, “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.” He also stressed the need to invest in young Nigerians, adding, “We need to build a future for our youth. item.title: [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to rule Nigerians following his recent visit to the holy mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. President Tinubu, while speaking with journalists, said he felt fulfilled after observing prayers at the holy mosque in Ka’aba. “I feel fulfilled and grateful to Almighty Allah for giving us the opportunity and the health. The day went very well. “The prayer is for Allah to convert our diversity. Nigeria is full of diversity. It is made up of all the faiths. May Allah convert all the diversity to prosperity for the country. That is my prayer”. Speaking on his requests while there, Tinubu noted that God had granted him the “wisdom to continue to serve Nigerians”. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the president of this great country. On commitment to Nigeria, President Tinubu noted that his commitment is “higher” and determined to bring prosperity. “My commitment is higher, and committed to bringing prosperity. To develop the country consistently with the wish of Allah and the support of the people”. He enjoined all to serve Allah and be guided by their consciences. “It is important to put Allah first. Then follow your conscience, follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness.” He reiterated that the economy was out of the woods and that the reforms were yielding good results. “The foundation is solid. The economy has come out of the dark tunnel. It is inspiring. We need to build the future for our youths. “If we don’t invest for their future, in 50 years from now, how do we want to be remembered as leaders? I am not looking for anything else.” He thanked management of the Ka’abha for granting him access to the holy mountain, saying that it was a historical moment for him. He assured Nigerians that the current economic challenges would soon be over. “I want to thank everyone for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe that the colour of the Ka’aba was green-white-green. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as a leader of the delegation. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome it with faith in the Almighty. “I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal crown prince. It is their honour to have allowed me to enter the Ka’aba. It is history.” The post [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse from Buhari — Plateau gov
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu inherited a Nigerian economy that was “tottering on the brink of collapse” from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Mutfwang stated this on Monday during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Campaign Council in Jos, where he also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria, tottering on the brink of collapse, Nigeria that could not service its external debts, Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home.” “And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria, because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.” “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades.” “Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” he said. Mutfwang further alleged that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming that more than N30 trillion was printed. “When the President took over in 2023, the government that he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy, and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion, which went down the drain.” “Today, by the grace of God, the Central Bank has stabilised, and that deficit has been done away with,” the governor said. On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. item.title: Oyedepo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍⁠​‌⁠​‍‌​tasks Africa with indigenous solutions to challenges
item.description: The Chancellor of Covenant University, Ota, Ogun, Dr David Oyedepo, has urged African countries to look inward and deploy indigenous solutions to address the continent’s numerous challenges. Oyedepo gave the advice in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Ota. He said that developing homegrown solutions to local challenges was the way forward for Africa to reduce its heavy dependence on foreign countries. “Man is created to solve his problems wherever he is planted. Therefore, African countries should provide solutions to their challenges without constantly seeking foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor said that Africa’s slow pace of development was not because its people were Black but largely because they were blind to their potential. ‘’Africans should take absolute responsibility for their destiny,” he said. Oyedepo attributed the continent’s inability to adequately address its challenges to what he described as a “what will happen will happen” mentality. According to him, the mindset has contributed significantly to Africa’s present situation by discouraging proactive thinking and responsibility. He said that the greatness of any nation depended on the valuable contributions of individuals and organisations within its borders. ‘’Africa will make meaningful progress only when its countries recognise the importance of indigenous solutions and take responsibility for addressing their challenges rather than relying excessively on foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor urged African leaders and citizens to harness their local knowledge, resources and capabilities to drive sustainable development across the continent. item.title: Bauchi LGA chairman dies in auto crash after APM meeting
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Chairman of Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident while returning from an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) stakeholders’ meeting in Bauchi. Umar reportedly died on Sunday night when his private car crashed at Konkiyal Village in Darazo Local Government Area, about 100 kilometres from Bauchi metropolis. The late chairman was returning to Zaki after attending the political meeting when the accident occurred. Before his election as Zaki LGA chairman on August 17, 2026, Umar served as Director-General of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA. Reacting to his death, Governor Bala Mohammed expressed shock, describing the deceased as a dedicated public servant, committed grassroots politician and compassionate leader whose contributions to public service and community development would remain indelible in the history of the state. In a condolence message issued by his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor said Umar’s tenure at SEMA was marked by his commitment to alleviating the suffering of vulnerable citizens and providing timely interventions to communities affected by emergencies and humanitarian challenges. Mohammed added that as chairman of Zaki Local Government, the deceased demonstrated commitment to grassroots development through initiatives aimed at empowering youths and women, improving livelihoods and promoting inclusive development. He described the death as a devastating loss to the deceased’s family, the people of Zaki and Bauchi State, particularly the public service and local government administration. The governor urged the family, political associates, friends and people of Zaki Local Government to find strength and comfort in Almighty Allah during the difficult period. The funeral prayer is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026, at 2pm at the Palace of the District Head, Mur Mur, Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State. item.title: [Updated] Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
item.description: Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline. “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei. “We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.” He said an exchange of messages was ongoing with the United States via mediators and that “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands. “Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages.” Since the Middle East war broke out in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital energy conduit for shipping. It regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross the strait without its authorisation, while the US has in retaliation imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports. In September, Iran initially proposed a seven-day plan that it conveyed to the US through Qatar, which would have seen Tehran reopen Hormuz on the sixth day after the US met Iranian demands. Those demands include ending the Middle East war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transit through the strait. He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region. Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran. The United States and Israel have in recent days also intensified threats to renew attacks on Iran amid crucial elections in both countries. On Saturday, US President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. “Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” said Baqaei during a foreign ministry briefing Monday. item.title: Traders hail Gbonse Foundation’s impact as organisation marks first anniversary
item.description: Traders benefiting from Gbonse Foundation for Economic Development have praised its accessible loans and low interest rates, saying the financial support has helped them grow their businesses and encouraged them to introduce other traders to the organisation. The traders spoke at the foundation’s first anniversary celebration held on Friday at its Igando office in Lagos, where beneficiaries shared their experiences and commended the organisation for its financial support. A foodstuff trader, Mercy Okoh, said she was happy to be associated with the foundation because its loans were genuine and had helped her business. “If you collect their N50,000, the money will multiply. This one year they have been wonderful. I have brought people to join the foundation and they have never regretted,” she said. Similarly, Tope Gbuyiwo, a trader in plastics and kitchen utensils at the foundation’s Ijegun branch, praised its low interest rates, saying she had benefited from successive loans. “I initially collected N200,000 and I’ve paid back. Now I’ve taken N250,000 loan. If I didn’t make profit, I wouldn’t see the advantage. So, I’ve brought people to join the foundation,” she said. Another beneficiary, Maureen Enaninhian, who trades in shoes and operates a point-of-sale business, said the foundation’s affordable lending conditions changed her perception of borrowing. “I don’t usually take loans. But the low interest rate Gbonse Foundation offers triggered me. It’s like they’re giving us free money and we don’t struggle or borrow to pay back,” she said. Established on October 25, 2025, Gbonse Foundation has supported individuals, families, traders, church members, women and schoolchildren across Igando, Egan, Odo, Ikotun and Ijegun communities through free medical outreaches, welfare assistance, educational initiatives and accessible loan services. Speaking at the event, business leader and keynote speaker from the foundation’s head office, Imafidon Omorodion, said the organisation was looking forward to expanding its operations and reaching more beneficiaries in the coming years. “The future is looking bright and we expect that this one year serves as a learning curve for the foundation and for the team at large. In the coming years, we expect expansion, hope to have more branches and overall meet more prospective beneficiaries of this laudable project,” Mr Omorodion told journalists. He acknowledged that the foundation’s collaboration with market associations and unions had yet to reach its desired level but described the relationship as progressive. “Our partnership with market associations and unions is not where we want it to be but it has been a progressive one. We are hoping it gets better in the coming years and we’re able to empower more women and have a wider reach to cover more demographics,” he added. item.title: Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu
item.description: Billionaire industrialist and Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has described his entry into the Holy Kaaba alongside President Bola Tinubu as a rare spiritual privilege and an experience he would cherish for the rest of his life. Rabiu disclosed this in a Facebook post on Sunday night, sharing a photograph of himself with Tinubu He wrote, “Some moments in life are beyond words, moments that touch the soul and remain forever engraved in the heart. “Alhamdulillah, today I was profoundly humbled and blessed to be among those granted the extraordinary honour of entering the Holy Kaaba alongside His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. “It was a once-in-a-lifetime blessing, an honour beyond measure, and a moment of divine grace that will remain etched in my heart for as long as I live.” Rabiu said his prayers at the sacred site extended beyond himself and his family to Nigeria, expressing hope for lasting peace, unity and prosperity in the country. He added, “In that most sacred of places, my thoughts and prayers were not only for myself and my family, but for our entire nation. “May Almighty Allah accept our prayers and bless our beloved nation with lasting peace, unity, and prosperity.” Rabiu was among the delegation that accompanied Tinubu to Makkah for Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage, on Friday, which included Oando Group Chief Executive Officer, Wale Tinubu, state governors and other senior government officials. Speaking at a dinner hosted for members of the delegation in Makkah on Saturday, Rabiu pledged the continued support of the business community for the administration and thanked the president for the rare spiritual opportunity. Tinubu had also told journalists after performing the Umrah that he felt fulfilled, describing the experience as spiritual.
